anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Optimizer-input metadata (row counts, histograms, correlations) is stale or incomplete, causing systematic cardinality misestimation and sub-optimal plan choices.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Engine memory regions (buffer pool, work areas, plan cache, background heaps) expand beyond the safe envelope of the host, provoking OS pressure, paging, or OOM events.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly : Standbys or downstream consumers cannot receive or apply log records at the rate produced by the primary, creating widening log-position gaps and retention of unrecycled log segments.

When these three root causes manifest together, the system exhibits a compound failure pattern: the optimizer repeatedly selects memory-hungry or parallel plans due to inaccurate statistics, inflating per-query work buffers and hash tables; this enlarges overall memory consumption, drives the database process into paging and stalls, and further slows local log generation and background I/O. The impaired primary now produces transaction logs in bursts with uneven latency, while replicas—already lagging—fall further behind because their replay threads contend for scarce memory and suffer the same mis-estimated plans. Observable symptoms therefore include: 1) dramatic divergence between estimated and actual rows in both primary and replica plans, 2) resident-set size and swap usage climbing in lock-step with plan cache and work-area footprints, 3) steep replication delay and unrecycled WAL/redo segments exhausting primary storage, 4) intermittent query timeouts, replica read staleness, and destabilising failover readiness.

Causally, stale statistics can trigger memory pressure by choosing plans that favor large in-memory sorts, hashes, or excessive parallelism. The resulting memory allocation anomaly not only degrades local execution but also starves the replication sender and receiver processes, slowing log shipping and apply throughput. Growing replication lag, in turn, prevents log file recycling, expanding the I/O footprint and exacerbating memory pressure through larger buffer-pool churn. Meanwhile, delayed replicas keep their own statistics ever more outdated, reinforcing the optimizer statistics anomaly on the replay side. Thus the three root causes reinforce each other in a feedback loop that degrades query performance, memory stability, and replication health simultaneously.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the amount of time with no network activity after which the operating system should send a TCP keepalive message to the client.
entry.trigger_condition: A TCP client connection has no network activity longer than tcp_keepalives_idle on systems supporting TCP_KEEPIDLE or an equivalent socket option.
entry.workload_impact: Starts TCP keepalive probing for an otherwise idle client connection; together with interval and count settings this can lead to dead connection detection.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
